Empirical Research Plan

1. Identification Strategy  
I will use a regression-discontinuity design (RDD) centered on the 50 percent vote-share threshold that determines whether a union is certified.  
Why RDD?  
• The treatment decision (certification) is an explicit, deterministic function of one continuous running variable (union yes-vote share).  
• Firms that win or lose by a razor-thin margin are plausibly similar in every respect except for certification status, giving us as‐good-as-random assignment in a narrow neighborhood of the cutoff.  
• The design delivers a transparently local causal effect that does not rely on parallel-trend assumptions and is tailor-made for “close elections” questions.

2. Treatment and Control  
Treatment variable  
Treated = 1 if the election outcome at time t pushed the union yes-vote share ≥ 0.50; 0 otherwise.  

Control group  
Firms whose election vote share fell just below 0.50.  

Treatment timing / event date  
Event date = certification election date. Outcomes will be measured in event time (k years relative to election, k = −5,…,+10).  

Running variable and cutoff  
Running variable r = yes_votes / total_valid_votes (or eligible voters). Cutoff c = 0.50.  
If some post-election legal challenges occasionally overturn results, the design becomes fuzzy; we can treat certification status as endogenous and use the 50 percent rule as an instrument.

3. Key Identifying Assumptions  
A1. Local continuity of potential outcomes at the cutoff.  
   – Plausible: vote share is determined by hundreds of individual workers; small shocks near 50 percent are hard to target strategically.  
A2. No precise manipulation of vote share (“sorting”).  
   – Plausible but testable with a McCrary density test.  
A3. Stable unit treatment value (no spillovers across firms within the bandwidth).  
   – Likely reasonable because certification applies to a single bargaining unit within a firm.  
A4. Treatment actually changes because of passing the cutoff (first-stage relevance, in a fuzzy RD).  
   – Almost mechanical, though rare challenges and decertifications can attenuate the first stage.  
A5. Outcome measurement is not affected by differential attrition at the cutoff.  
   – Must verify that firm survival is not discontinuously different just above/below 50 percent.

4. Threats to Identification and Mitigation  
T1. Manipulation of the running variable (turnout buying, ballot challenges).  
   – Conduct McCrary density test; inspect bunching; drop elections with documented irregularities.  
T2. Differential pre-trends in firm outcomes (e.g., unions target declining firms).  
   – Include pre-election covariates as controls; estimate event-time graphs to confirm no pre-treatment discontinuity.  
T3. Attrition / firm exit.  
   – Test for discontinuity in survival probability; use inverse-probability weighting or Lee bounds if exit is non-random.

5. R Code Outline  

```r
# --- PACKAGES ---------------------------------------------------------------
library(tidyverse)
library(fixest)      # for high-dimensional FE & robust se
library(rdrobust)    # main RD estimator
library(rddensity)   # McCrary test

# --- DATA ------------------------------------------------------------------
elections <- read_csv("nlrb_elections_1984_2001.csv")     # election data
firm_out   <- read_csv("firm_outcomes_panel.csv")         # outcomes (employment, wages, etc.)

# --- VARIABLE CONSTRUCTION -------------------------------------------------
elections <- elections %>% 
  mutate(vote_share = yes_votes / total_valid_votes,
         treated = as.integer(vote_share >= 0.5),
         margin  = vote_share - 0.5)            # running variable centered at cutoff

# Keep only the first election per firm during the window to avoid multi-treatment issues
elections_first <- elections %>% 
  arrange(firm_id, election_date) %>% 
  group_by(firm_id) %>% 
  slice(1) %>% 
  ungroup()

# Merge with panel of outcomes (assumed yearly)
panel <- firm_out %>% 
  left_join(elections_first %>% select(firm_id, election_date, margin, treated),
            by = "firm_id") %>% 
  mutate(event_year = year - lubridate::year(election_date))

# --- MAIN RDD ESTIMATION (cross-sectional, local linear) -------------------
# Use data within ±0.05 bandwidth around cutoff
band <- 0.05
rd_sample <- elections_first %>% filter(abs(margin) <= band)

rd_out <- rdrobust(y = rd_sample$employment_level_next_year,
                   x = rd_sample$margin,
                   covs = rd_sample %>% 
                          select(log_assets_pre, industry_fe, state_fe))

summary(rd_out)

# --- EVENT-STUDY RDD (difference-in-discontinuities) -----------------------
# Local sample with panel structure
panel_local <- panel %>% filter(abs(margin) <= band, between(event_year, -5, 10))

# Event-time dummies
panel_local <- panel_local %>% 
  mutate(event_factor = factor(event_year))

est <- feols(log_employment ~ treated * event_factor + log_assets_pre + i(year) | firm_id,
             data = panel_local, cluster = ~firm_id)

iplot(est, main = "Dynamic treatment effects around the cutoff")

# --- ROBUSTNESS CHECK ------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Different bandwidth
rd_out_bw <- rdrobust(y = rd_sample$employment_level_next_year,
                      x = rd_sample$margin, h = 0.03)
summary(rd_out_bw)

# 2. Density test
dens_test <- rddensity(x = elections_first$margin)
summary(dens_test)
```

6. Expected Results  
Based on the existing theoretical and descriptive literature:  
• Wages: positive discontinuity (+2 – 4 percent).  
• Employment: small negative (−1 – 3 percent).  
• Productivity / value added per worker: ambiguous; could rise if unions reduce turnover, or fall if work rules bind. My prior is a near-zero average effect.  
Economic magnitude is expected to be modest because most bargaining units are small relative to the overall firm, and only a minority of close-win unions ultimately secure first contracts.

7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (1 = clearly satisfied, 0 = questionable)  
C1. No manipulation of running variable ……… 0.8  
C2. Covariate balance at cutoff …………………… 1  
C3. Correct functional form / optimal bandwidth … 1  
C4. No other discontinuous policies at 50 % ……… 0.9  
C5. Robustness across bandwidths & specs ……… 1  

(Overall score = 4.7 / 5 → strong but must verify manipulation and survival.)
